banner.name: active_namespace
banner.desc: top line 'active_namespace: ns-XXXX' + note; a trailing '[reminder] your namespace ...' is appended too

section.name: last expression
section.desc: repr of last expression; shown ONLY when stdout is empty

section.name: artifacts
section.desc: Markdown links to new/changed ./workspace files; images as ![](), else []()

namespaceParam.desc: Mandatory on execution tools. Per-conversation isolation; see 09-namespace-routing.md.
namespaceParam.rule: Pass 'new' (or empty) on the first call to mint a fresh ns-XXXX.
Reuse the exact active_namespace value returned, on every later call.
id source priority: MCP _meta conversation id (future) > this arg > minted.

injected.name: ctx
injected.desc: FastMCP-injected, hidden from schema; carries future _meta hook

tool.name: execute_python_code
tool.description: Run Python in the namespace's stateful IPython kernel. Variables/imports persist across calls within that namespace.

input.param: Python source to execute. Use print() to return values; save plots to ./workspace.

tool.name: run_python_file
tool.description: Run an existing .py file from ./workspace as a script (runpy.run_path with run_name='__main__'); its __main__ block runs. The file's top-level names are merged into the kernel namespace afterwards.

input.param: Path to a .py file INSIDE ./workspace. Accepts bare name, ./workspace/ prefix, or absolute path within the workspace.

isolation.error: execution_status: ERROR, message contains "outside the workspace"
execution_status: ERROR, message contains "is not a .py file"; checked before the kernel is touched

tool.name: write_workspace_file
tool.description: Write text content verbatim to a file inside ./workspace. Exists so a model never has to generate Python that quotes its own source in order to save a file -- the self-referential nesting that most reliably breaks small/mid-size models. Takes NO namespace: it holds no state and the workspace is shared.

input.param: Path relative to ./workspace, e.g. "fib.py" or "reports/out.md". A leading "./workspace/", "workspace/" or "/workspace/" is stripped.
Exact text to write. UTF-8, no BOM, newline="\n" so Windows text mode does not turn LF into CRLF.
Replace an existing file instead of refusing.

section.name: artifacts
section.desc: same Markdown links as the execution tools (snapshot/diff); empty diff is reported as a silent-failure warning

section.name: next
section.desc: for a .py target, a run_python_file(...) hint that also re-surfaces the namespace requirement

isolation.rule: Resolved via _resolve_new_workspace_path(); the target need not exist, so containment is checked on the PARENT after resolve().
Subdirectories are created only after the containment check passes.
isolation.error: write_status: ERROR, "pass a path relative to ./workspace"
write_status: ERROR, "reserved device name" -- Windows would otherwise accept the write and discard it
write_status: ERROR, "already exists"; message states the fix (overwrite=true or a new filename)

limit.note: 0 disables; no append mode by design

tool.name: list_workspace_files
tool.description: List every file under ./workspace with size and extension, or a note if empty.

tool.name: reset_kernel_state
tool.description: Restart ONE namespace's kernel, clearing that conversation's in-memory state. Workspace files kept; other namespaces untouched.

embeddedRules.notAppliedReason: _RULES opens by demanding a namespace these tools do not take; adding ~500 tokens of kernel rules would undo the low-load design
embeddedRules.rule: No pip/apt/conda, no network. All libraries pre-installed.
matplotlib savefig+close (no show); plotly write_html; save pptx/pdf/docx/html into ./workspace.
On stderr error, fix and retry.

toolBoundaries.note: overlapping tools are how small models pick the wrong one; keep these pointers in sync with the descriptions
toolBoundaries.boundary: "To simply SAVE text or code to a file without running it, use write_workspace_file instead -- it is simpler and needs no namespace."
Appended to the response for a .py target: "Next: run it with run_python_file(...)".
